text:
jess-support: :rotating_light: Customer X reporting huge spike in 5xx from hosted API since ~09:10 UTC, multiple customers complaining about timeouts and failed billable operations. Support case #45912. Sample error: 'gateway timeout 504' and '502 upstream reset'.

mike-oncall: I'm seeing cluster alerts too, started ~09:07. P95 latency up, 502/503 ratio up. Investigating canary traffic slice.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered by sarah-platform at 2025-07-06T09:05:12Z — rollout id: r-20250706-2981, canary=10% -> 30%. Config change: route-tagging:enable=true.

sarah-platform: Confirmed — we flipped a routing tag flag to enable per-tenant sticky routes for the kernelpath experiment. New selector leaked to canary routers. Rolling back now if needed.

raj-sre: Logs show auth header truncation for a subset of requests hitting new route path. Example trace ids: trace=0f3a.. Logs: ```ERROR auth.go:142 header truncated, len=1024 -> rejected``` That causes our gateway to return 5xx in some code paths.

ben-eng: Repro steps I ran locally: curl -> proxy -> gets 502 when header length over 1k with the new route. Steps: 
1) set header X-Client-Meta to 1100 chars
2) POST /v1/generate -> gateway returns 502 immediately
3) reverting route-tagging locally fixes it.

lina-pm: We have two paying customers on that canary slice and one support SLA ticket escalated to priority. CS is asking for ETA and whether we should pause rollout.

alice-ops: Pause request acknowledged. mike-oncall, can you hold traffic and coordinate rollback? Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/canary-rollback (see step 2 for staged rollback).

mike-oncall: Doing hold now — setting canary weight to 0 for r-20250706-2981. Command: `redwoodctl rollout adjust --id r-20250706-2981 --weight 0`

deploy-bot: rollout r-20250706-2981 weight adjusted -> 0 by mike-oncall at 2025-07-06T09:20:05Z :white_check_mark:

raj-sre: After weight drop, error rates dropped in ~45s at edge. Still seeing some 504s from upstream cache priming but much lower.

jess-support: Confirmed with Customer X that traffic is restored and most requests succeed. They still saw several failed billing webhook retries earlier, CS asking if we should credit retry charges.

ben-eng: Root cause appears to be the route-tagging selector path triggering a different auth normalization code path that mishandled long headers. Patch in PR #4823 ready — adds header truncation guard and better error return (400) for clients instead of causing gateway 5xx.

sarah-platform: Moving PR to hotfix and will cut a canary rollback patch. Need approvers: @ben-eng, @raj-sre review.

alice-ops: Coordination note: Notify billing and CS to hold off auto-collection for affected webhooks for window 09:05–09:22 UTC. Also file a billing credit pre-approval.

lina-pm: I'll notify the customers and open an incident status update. Action items: 1) ship hotfix 2) run targeted canary for the two tenants 3) follow up on billing credits.

mike-oncall: Closing timeline note: canary flip caused 5xx spike, rollback at 09:20 removed majority of errors. Hotfix + targeted canary recommended.

deploy-bot: hotfix build b-20250706-12 created from PR #4823.

raj-sre: After hotfix deploy to a tiny canary (1%) will watch auth error rate and gateway 5xx. Will post metrics in 5m.

jess-support: Thanks team — keeping ticket open until hotfix verifies and CS confirms billing scope. :pray:
